newsitem.title: USA: Total CEO sees refining costs falling.
newsitem.headline: Total CEO sees refining costs falling.

text.p: French oil company Total will see European refining costs fall by eight percent this year and next, the company's chief executive said Tuesday.

Thierry Desmarest, in New Orleans for the Howard Weill conference on the oil industry, said Total's European refining costs are expected to fall by $1 per tonne of feedstock processed in both 1997 and 1998, down from last year's $12.4 per tonne (about $1.69 per barrel).
He told the conference that refining margins in Europe were close to the level seen last year.
"Our refining operations in Europe have been helped somewhat by the higher value of the U.S. dollar versus the french franc," Desmarest said.

Total in January reported a 50 percent rise in 1996 net income to 5.6 billion francs ($1 billion). Desmarest reiterated that the company plans to pay in cash only the increased dividend due in May. Total said last month that it will increase its dividend 21 percent to 10.5 francs and said it won't seek to exercise its option to pay out in shares.
Desmarest said the Total still has various options to pursue for its North American refining subsidiary, Total Petroleum (North America) Ltd (TOPNA), but he declined to comment on specifics.
"I don't want to comment in detail at this stage. We have to look at different possibilities," he said.

In February, the Wall Street Journal said Total had reached agreement to sell its 55 percent stake in TOPNA to Ultramar Diamond Shamrock for $830 million, but TOPNA treasurer Douglas Kerner said in response that the company still had options to sell, merge or form a joint venture.
((--David Chance, James Pierpoint, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1620))
